question: Which was the first socio-religious organisation established in Bombay in 1840 to work for the annihilation of caste?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Paramhans Mandali.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Paramhans Mandali was founded in Bombay in 1840 as a secret socio-religious reform society aimed at breaking down caste distinctions among Hindus. (परमहंस मंडली — जाति उन्मूलन)

 

• Its members took a pledge to dine together across caste lines and to work against idolatry and caste rigidity; Dadoba Pandurang is closely associated with its founding and ideology.

 

• Because open defiance of caste norms invited social ostracism, the Mandali functioned secretly, with members outwardly conforming to caste practice while inwardly rejecting it.

 

• A later prominent member, Karsandas Mulji, went on to found the reformist journal *Satya Prakash* and was central to the famous Maharaj Libel Case (1862) against caste and religious orthodoxy.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Paramhans Mandali is considered a precursor to later reform movements such as the Prarthana Samaj, founded in Bombay in 1867, which carried forward similar reformist ideals openly.

 

NOTE

 

• Satyashodhak Samaj (Option 1): Founded by Jyotirao Phule in 1873 at Pune, not Bombay 1840, to fight caste oppression and Brahmanical dominance.

 

• Vishwa Jain Sangathan (Option 2): A modern-day Jain community organisation, unrelated to this 1840 Bombay reform movement.

 

• Dharma Sabha (Option 4): Founded by Radhakanta Deb in 1830 in Calcutta as a conservative organisation opposing reformist measures like the abolition of Sati, not a Bombay-based anti-caste body.

question: Which of the following is NOT applicable to force?
option_1: Force may change the shape of an object
option_2: Force may change the direction of a moving object
option_3: Force may increase the mass of the object
option_4: Force may make an object move
solution_text:
The correct answer is Force may increase the mass of the object.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A force is a push or pull that can change an object's state of motion (start, stop, speed up, slow down) or its shape/size, but it cannot change the mass of the object. (बल — द्रव्यमान अपरिवर्तित)

 

• Mass is an intrinsic property of matter, a measure of the quantity of matter in a body; in classical (Newtonian) mechanics it stays constant regardless of the forces acting on the object.

 

• Applying force can deform an object (e.g., squeezing a rubber ball), change its direction (e.g., a bat hitting a ball), or set a stationary body into motion, but none of these effects alter how much matter the object contains.

 

• This is consistent with Newton's Second Law, F = ma, where mass (m) is treated as a fixed property of the object used to relate force and acceleration, not something force itself modifies.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Force is measured in newtons (N) in the SI system; 1 N is the force that produces an acceleration of 1 m/s² in a 1 kg mass.

 

• Force is a vector quantity, having both magnitude and direction, which is why it can change the direction of motion of a body.

 

NOTE

 

• Force may change the shape of an object (Option 1): True — deforming forces change shape, as in stretching a spring.

 

• Force may change the direction of a moving object (Option 2): True — e.g., a centripetal force changes the direction of a body moving in a circle.

 

• Force may make an object move (Option 4): True — an unbalanced force acting on a stationary object sets it in motion.

question: In the year 2021, the Department of Public Enterprises has now been made part of the __________ Ministry, to speed up the privatisation process and exercise greater financial control over the state-run-enterprises.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Finance.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In July 2021, the Department of Public Enterprises (DPE) was moved out of the Ministry of Heavy Industries and brought under the Ministry of Finance. (लोक उद्यम विभाग — वित्त मंत्रालय)

 

• The move was intended to give the government greater financial control over Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) and to align policy-making on public enterprises more closely with the government's privatisation and disinvestment drive.

 

• DPE is the nodal department for all administrative matters concerning CPSEs and lays down policy on their performance, autonomy, and accountability.

 

• Placing DPE alongside the Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM), which also handles disinvestment, within the same ministry helped streamline strategic disinvestment decisions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• DIPAM (Department of Investment and Public Asset Management) is also under the Ministry of Finance and is the nodal body for the Central Government's disinvestment programme.

 

• The New Public Sector Enterprise Policy (2021) classifies CPSEs into strategic and non-strategic sectors, guiding the extent of government presence in each.

 

NOTE

 

• Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises (Option 2): This was DPE's earlier ministerial affiliation, before the 2021 shift.

 

• Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (Option 1): This ministry deals with MSME promotion, not oversight of large public sector enterprises.

 

• Commerce and Industry (Option 4): This ministry handles trade policy and industrial promotion, not public enterprise administration.

question: Competitive behaviour and competitive market structure are _______ related.
solution_text:
The correct answer is inversely.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In economics, competitive behaviour (the intensity of rivalry firms display, such as price wars or aggressive advertising) and competitive market structure (the number of firms and degree of concentration in a market) are said to be inversely related. (प्रतिस्पर्धी व्यवहार — विपरीत संबंध)

 

• In a market structure that is highly competitive (many small firms, as in perfect competition), individual firms are price takers with little market power, so there is little scope or need for aggressive strategic "competitive behaviour" against rivals.

 

• In contrast, in less competitive, more concentrated structures such as oligopoly, a small number of firms with significant market power often display intense competitive behaviour — price wars, advertising battles, strategic rivalry — precisely because each firm's actions strongly affect the others.

 

• This distinction between market structure (the objective count/concentration of firms) and market conduct/behaviour (how firms actually act) is a standard theme in industrial economics.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• This idea forms part of the classic Structure-Conduct-Performance (SCP) framework used to analyse markets in industrial organisation economics.

 

• Monopoly, at the other extreme of market structure, typically shows the least competitive behaviour, since there are no rivals to compete against.

 

NOTE

 

• not (Option 1): Incorrect — the two concepts are related, just inversely rather than unrelated.

 

• directly (Option 2): Incorrect — more competitive structures do not show more competitive behaviour; the relationship runs the opposite way.

 

• proportionately (Option 4): Incorrect — there is no fixed proportional relationship; the relationship is characterised as inverse, not a direct proportion.

question: How many basic talams are there in Indian Classical Carnatic music?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 7.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Carnatic (South Indian classical) music recognises 7 basic talas, together called the Suladi Sapta Talas. (सप्त ताल — कर्नाटक संगीत)

 

• The seven basic talas are: Dhruva, Matya, Rupaka, Jhampa, Triputa, Ata, and Eka.

 

• Each of these seven talas, when combined with five possible jati (gati) variations (Tisra, Chaturasra, Khanda, Misra, Sankirna) based on the count of the *laghu* anga, theoretically expands into 35 talas, a scheme systematised as part of Carnatic music theory.

 

• The tala framework provides the rhythmic cycle within which Carnatic compositions are set, marked using hand gestures (kriyas) of anudruta, druta, and laghu.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Among the 35 (or including other extensions, 108) tala variants, Adi Tala (a form of Triputa tala in chaturasra jati, an 8-beat cycle) is the most commonly used tala in Carnatic music practice and performance.

 

• Purandara Dasa, regarded as the father of Carnatic music, is credited with systematising the pedagogical structure that underlies the tala and raga system taught today.

 

NOTE

 

• 37 (Option 1), 21 (Option 3), 11 (Option 4): None of these correspond to the recognised count of basic Carnatic talas, which is fixed at seven (Sapta Talas).

question: Which of the following is NOT a condition for acquiring the citizenship of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Holding property.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Citizenship Act, 1955 lays down the modes by which a person can acquire Indian citizenship: by birth, by descent, by registration, by naturalisation, and by incorporation of territory. (नागरिकता अधिनियम, 1955 — संपत्ति नहीं)

 

• Merely holding property in India is not a recognised legal basis for acquiring citizenship under the Act.

 

• Descent allows a person born outside India to acquire citizenship if a parent was an Indian citizen at the time of birth, subject to conditions on registration with an Indian consulate.

 

• Registration allows certain categories of persons (such as those of Indian origin, or a foreign spouse of an Indian citizen) to acquire citizenship by applying to the prescribed authority, and can involve a domicile/residence requirement in some categories.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Naturalisation allows a foreigner to acquire Indian citizenship after fulfilling residency and other qualifying conditions laid out in the Third Schedule of the Act.

 

• Citizenship by incorporation of territory occurs when a new territory becomes part of India and its people are declared citizens by government notification (e.g., Sikkim, Puducherry, Goa).

 

NOTE

 

• Descent (Option 2): A valid statutory mode of acquiring citizenship, hence not the answer.

 

• Registration (Option 3): A valid statutory mode of acquiring citizenship, hence not the answer.

 

• Domicile (Option 4): While residence-linked, it can factor into registration/naturalisation eligibility conditions and is not, by itself, excluded the way "holding property" is; the Act does not recognise property ownership as a route to citizenship at all.

question: The catchphrase of which census is ‘Our census, our future’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2011.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Census of India 2011, the 15th national census, adopted the slogan/catchphrase "Our Census, Our Future". (जनगणना 2011 — हमारी जनगणना, हमारा भविष्य)

 

• Census 2011 was conducted in two phases: house listing and housing census (April-September 2010), followed by the population enumeration (9-28 February 2011).

 

• It was headed by C. Chandramouli, the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India, and covered the country's population as of 1 March 2011 (0 hours reference).

 

• India's population as per the 2011 Census was recorded as approximately 121.09 crore (1.21 billion).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Census 2011 was the first census to include a National Population Register (NPR) exercise alongside house listing, and it introduced biometric data collection for residents.

 

• The Census of India is conducted decennially by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, under the Ministry of Home Affairs, under the Census Act, 1948.

 

NOTE

 

• 1981, 1991, 2001 (Options 1, 2, 3): These were earlier decennial censuses of India but none of them used the "Our Census, Our Future" slogan, which is specific to the 2011 Census.

question: The Gulf of Khambhat, the Gulf of Kutch and Gangetic delta provide ideal conditions for utilising ________energy.
solution_text:
The correct answer is tidal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tidal energy is generated by harnessing the rise and fall of ocean tides; it requires locations with a large tidal range. (ज्वारीय ऊर्जा — गुजरात व सुंदरबन)

 

• The Gulf of Khambhat (Cambay) and the Gulf of Kutch in Gujarat, along with the Gangetic (Sundarbans) delta in West Bengal, have among the highest tidal ranges in India, making them ideal candidate sites for tidal power generation.

 

• The Gulf of Khambhat has the highest estimated tidal energy potential in India (reported tidal range up to about 11 metres), followed by the Gulf of Kutch.

 

• India's first attempted tidal power project (50 MW capacity) was proposed at the Gulf of Kutch, near Kandla, Gujarat.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Besides tidal sites, India has strong potential for wind energy along Gujarat, Tamil Nadu and Rajasthan's coasts and plains, and abundant solar energy potential across the Thar Desert region of Rajasthan.

 

• Globally, the La Rance Tidal Power Station in France was the first large-scale tidal power plant, commissioned in 1966.

 

NOTE

 

• solar (Option 1): Solar energy depends on sunlight exposure, best suited to arid/desert regions like Rajasthan, not specifically these tidal gulf/delta locations.

 

• atomic (Option 2): Nuclear/atomic power plants require access to large volumes of water for cooling and are sited based on different criteria (e.g. Kakrapar in Gujarat), not tidal range.

 

• geo thermal (Option 3): Geothermal energy depends on underground heat sources (e.g., Puga Valley, Ladakh; Manikaran, Himachal Pradesh), unrelated to tidal range along these gulfs and delta.

question: How many times has India hosted the ICC Men’s T-20 Cricket World Cup as of 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As of 2023, India had hosted the ICC Men's T20 World Cup on only one occasion, as the sole host. (आईसीसी टी20 विश्व कप — भारत 2016)

 

• That edition was the 2016 ICC World Twenty20, held in India from 8 March to 3 April 2016, won by the West Indies, who defeated England in the final at Eden Gardens, Kolkata.

 

• India also hosted the inaugural 2006 ICC Champions Trophy and multiple editions of the ICC Cricket World Cup (ODI) (1987, 1996 as co-host, 2011 as co-host, 2023 as sole host), but these are distinct tournaments from the men's T20 World Cup.

 

• India is set to co-host the next Men's T20 World Cup with Sri Lanka in future editions, but as of 2023 India's sole hosting tally for this specific tournament stood at one.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India won the inaugural ICC World Twenty20 in 2007 in South Africa, defeating Pakistan in the final.

 

• The 2021 ICC Men's T20 World Cup was scheduled to be hosted by India but was relocated to the UAE and Oman due to the COVID-19 pandemic situation in India at the time.

 

NOTE

 

• 3, 4, 2 (Options 1, 2, 3): India has not hosted the Men's T20 World Cup that many times as of 2023; only the 2016 edition was hosted on Indian soil.

question: ‘Reservation in promotion’ comes under which Article of the Constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 16 (4A).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 16(4A) of the Constitution of India empowers the State to make provisions for reservation in matters of promotion, with consequential seniority, for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in public employment, if the State believes they are inadequately represented. (अनुच्छेद 16(4क) — पदोन्नति में आरक्षण)

 

• This clause was inserted by the 77th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1995, following the Supreme Court's ruling in *Indra Sawhney v. Union of India (1992)*, which had held that reservation could not extend to promotions under the original Article 16(4).

 

• Article 16 as a whole guarantees equality of opportunity in matters of public employment, and clause (4A) is a specific exception carved out for SC/ST promotion-based reservation.

 

• The 85th Amendment (2001) further clarified that consequential seniority would also apply to such promotions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 16(4) (distinct from 4A) provides for reservation of appointments/posts for backward classes not adequately represented in State services.

 

• Article 16(4B), inserted by the 81st Amendment, allows unfilled reserved vacancies of a year to be carried forward and treated as a separate class in the succeeding year, not subject to the 50% ceiling with that year's vacancies.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 15(3B) (Option 1): Relates to reservation for socially/educationally backward classes and SC/ST in admission to private educational institutions.

 

• Article 19(2) (Option 2): Provides for reasonable restrictions on the freedom of speech and expression, unrelated to reservation.

 

• Article 14(4A) (Option 3): There is no such provision — Article 14 (Right to Equality) has no clause 4A; this is a fabricated combination.

question: Who took oath as the Chief Minister of Karnataka, in May 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Siddaramaiah.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Siddaramaiah took oath as the Chief Minister of Karnataka on 20 May 2023, following the Indian National Congress's decisive victory in the 2023 Karnataka Legislative Assembly election. (सिद्धारमैया — कर्नाटक मुख्यमंत्री, मई 2023)

 

• This was Siddaramaiah's second stint as Chief Minister of Karnataka, having earlier served as CM from 2013 to 2018.

 

• D.K. Shivakumar, the Karnataka Congress president who had also been a contender for the top post, was made Deputy Chief Minister in the same government.

 

• The oath-taking ceremony was held at the Kanteerava Stadium, Bengaluru, attended by several opposition INDIA bloc leaders.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Congress swept the 2023 Karnataka elections, winning 135 of 224 seats, defeating the incumbent BJP government led by Basavaraj Bommai.

 

• Karnataka's Raj Bhavan (Governor at the time) was Thawar Chand Gehlot, who administered the oath of office.

 

NOTE

 

• Mallikarjun Kharge (Option 2): The national president of the Indian National Congress at the time, not the Karnataka CM.

 

• MK Stalin (Option 3): Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, not Karnataka.

 

• DK Sivakumar (Option 4): Became Deputy Chief Minister of Karnataka in this government, not the Chief Minister.

question:
Match the items in List I with those in List II.

List I

i. Balanced Growth Theory

ii. Big Push Theory

iii. Secular Deterioration

iv. Capital Goods and Heavy Industry

List II

a. Rosenstein Rodan

b. Feldman-Mahalanobis

c. Ragnar Nurkse

d. Prebisch-Singer
solution_text:
The correct answer is i-c, ii-a, iii-d, iv-b.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Balanced Growth Theory was propounded by Ragnar Nurkse, who argued that simultaneous investment across multiple sectors is needed to break the vicious circle of poverty (i-c). (संतुलित विकास सिद्धांत — रैगनर नर्क्स)

 

• The Big Push Theory was propounded by Paul Rosenstein-Rodan, who argued that a large, coordinated investment (a "big push") across industries is needed to overcome market failures and set underdeveloped economies on a growth path (ii-a).

 

• The theory of Secular Deterioration (of the terms of trade of primary-good-exporting countries) is associated with the Prebisch-Singer thesis, put forward independently by Raul Prebisch and Hans Singer (iii-d).

 

• The strategy emphasising Capital Goods and Heavy Industry as the basis of planned development is the Feldman-Mahalanobis model, which underpinned India's Second Five-Year Plan (iv-b).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Mahalanobis model, devised by statistician P.C. Mahalanobis, drew on the earlier work of Soviet economist Grigory Feldman, hence the joint name "Feldman-Mahalanobis model".

 

• The Prebisch-Singer thesis underpinned the case for import substitution industrialisation in developing countries during the mid-20th century.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (i-c, ii-d, iii-a, iv-b): Incorrectly swaps the Big Push and Secular Deterioration pairings.

 

• Option 2 (i-d, ii-a, iii-b, iv-c): Incorrectly assigns Balanced Growth to Prebisch-Singer and Secular Deterioration to Feldman-Mahalanobis.

 

• Option 4 (i-a, ii-b, iii-d, iv-c): Incorrectly assigns Balanced Growth to Rosenstein-Rodan and Big Push to Feldman-Mahalanobis.

question: As of 2022, which among of the following is the leading tidal energy generation site of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gulf of Kutch.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Among India's identified tidal energy sites, the Gulf of Kutch in Gujarat is recognised as the country's leading tidal energy generation site, having been chosen for India's first attempted commercial-scale tidal power project. (गल्फ ऑफ कच्छ — ज्वारीय ऊर्जा)

 

• A 50 MW tidal power project was proposed near Kandla, Gulf of Kutch, envisaged as India's first large tidal energy plant, developed with support from private and state agencies.

 

• The Gulf of Kutch benefits from a favourable tidal range (around 5 metres) and funnel-shaped coastal geometry, which concentrates tidal flow and makes it attractive for tidal barrage/turbine technology.

 

• India's National Institute of Ocean Technology (NIOT) and Gujarat state agencies have both identified the Gulf of Kutch as the most developed/prioritised site for tidal power among Indian locations.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Gulf of Khambhat, also in Gujarat, has an even higher tidal range (up to about 11 m) and larger theoretical potential, but has seen comparatively less project development than the Gulf of Kutch.

 

• India's total tidal energy potential is estimated at around 12,455 MW, concentrated mainly in the Gulf of Kutch, Gulf of Khambhat, and the Sundarbans.

 

NOTE

 

• Sunderbans (Option 1): Has tidal energy potential (estimated around 100 MW) but is much smaller in scale than the Gulf of Kutch site.

 

• Seashore of Maharashtra (Option 2): Not identified as a major tidal energy site; Maharashtra's coast lacks the funnel-shaped estuarine geography needed for high tidal range.

 

• Gulf of Mannar (Option 4): Known for its marine biodiversity and as a potential site for ocean thermal energy (OTEC) and wave energy studies, not for leading tidal power generation.

question: Which of the following is an example of multi-factor authentication for PC security?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fingerprint scan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Multi-factor authentication (MFA) verifies identity using more than one independent factor, typically drawn from: something you know (password/PIN), something you have (a security token/smartcard), and something you are (a biometric trait). (बहु-कारक प्रमाणीकरण — फिंगरप्रिंट)

 

• A fingerprint scan is a biometric authentication factor — an example of the "something you are" category — and is commonly combined with a password or PIN to implement MFA on PCs and devices.

 

• Among the given options, only the fingerprint scan represents an authentication mechanism at all; the others are security tools that protect a system but do not verify a user's identity through multiple factors.

 

• Modern laptops and phones frequently pair a password/PIN with fingerprint or facial recognition as a practical two-factor (multi-factor) authentication setup.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other biometric MFA factors include facial recognition, iris/retina scans, and voice recognition.

 

• One-Time Passwords (OTPs) sent to a registered mobile device are another widely used "something you have" factor in multi-factor authentication schemes.

 

NOTE

 

• Antivirus software (Option 1): Detects and removes malicious software; it is not an authentication mechanism.

 

• OS protection (Option 3): Refers to general operating-system-level security measures (permissions, updates, etc.), not an identity-verification factor.

 

• Firewall protection (Option 4): Filters network traffic to block unauthorised access; it does not authenticate a user's identity.

question: Which of the following is a feature of Directive Principles of State Policy, and also distinguishes it from Fundamental Rights?
option_1: It protects the interest of the individual.
solution_text:
The correct answer is It is non-justiciable.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSPs), contained in Part IV (Articles 36-51) of the Constitution, are explicitly declared non-justiciable by Article 37 — they cannot be enforced by any court of law. (राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्व — गैर-न्यायसंगत)

 

• This is the key feature that distinguishes DPSPs from Fundamental Rights: Fundamental Rights (Part III) are justiciable, meaning citizens can approach courts (directly the Supreme Court under Article 32, or High Courts under Article 226) to enforce them.

 

• Despite being non-justiciable, Article 37 also states that DPSPs are "fundamental in the governance of the country", and it is the duty of the State to apply these principles in making laws.

 

• DPSPs aim to promote the welfare and interest of society/the community as a whole (a Gandhian, socialist, and liberal blend of ideals) rather than protecting the individual, which is closer to the role of Fundamental Rights.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• DPSPs are inspired by the Irish Constitution, while most Fundamental Rights draw inspiration from the US Bill of Rights.

 

• Courts have used DPSPs to interpret the scope of Fundamental Rights in several landmark cases, even though DPSPs themselves cannot be directly enforced (e.g., in *Minerva Mills v. Union of India, 1980*, which discussed the harmony between Parts III and IV).

 

NOTE

 

• It protects the interest of the individual (Option 1): This better describes Fundamental Rights, which safeguard individual liberties; DPSPs are oriented towards the collective welfare of society.

 

• It is prohibitive in nature (Option 2): Fundamental Rights are largely prohibitive (restraining State action), while DPSPs are positive/affirmative directions to the State, not prohibitions.

 

• It is justiciable (Option 4): This is the opposite of the correct feature — DPSPs are specifically non-justiciable, unlike Fundamental Rights.

question: Which planet is the second largest planet in our solar system and also has the biggest and brightest rings around it?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Saturn.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Saturn is the second largest planet in the solar system after Jupiter, and is famed for having the largest, brightest, and most extensive ring system of any planet. (शनि — सौरमंडल का दूसरा सबसे बड़ा ग्रह)

 

• Saturn's rings are composed mainly of ice particles, with smaller amounts of rocky debris and dust, and span a huge diameter while being remarkably thin.

 

• Saturn is the sixth planet from the Sun and is classified, along with Jupiter, Uranus and Neptune, as a gas giant.

 

• Saturn has the lowest density of any planet in the solar system — less than water — meaning it would theoretically float if placed in a large enough body of water.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Saturn's largest moon, Titan, is the second-largest moon in the solar system and the only moon known to have a dense atmosphere.

 

• Both Uranus and Neptune also possess ring systems, but they are far fainter and less prominent than Saturn's.

 

NOTE

 

• Earth (Option 2): The third planet from the Sun; it is a small rocky planet with no ring system.

 

• Uranus (Option 3): The seventh planet from the Sun; it has a faint ring system, but is neither the second largest planet nor known for the biggest/brightest rings.

 

• Jupiter (Option 4): The largest planet in the solar system, but its ring system is very faint and not the most prominent — that distinction belongs to Saturn.

question: Which of the following muscles regulates the exit of food from the stomach into the small intestine?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sphincter.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The pyloric sphincter (a ring-like muscle located at the junction of the stomach and the duodenum, the first part of the small intestine) regulates the passage of partially digested food (chyme) from the stomach into the small intestine. (पाइलोरिक स्फिंक्टर — पेट से भोजन का निकास)

 

• A sphincter is a circular muscle that maintains constriction of a natural body passage or orifice and relaxes as required by normal physiological functioning, controlling the flow of contents through the passage.

 

• The pyloric sphincter opens intermittently to release small amounts of chyme into the duodenum, allowing time for digestive enzymes to act, and closes to prevent backflow.

 

• Other important human sphincters include the oesophageal sphincters (upper and lower, at the top and bottom of the food pipe) and the anal sphincter.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The lower oesophageal (cardiac) sphincter prevents backflow of stomach acid into the oesophagus; its malfunction is associated with acid reflux/GERD.

 

• The stomach itself is divided into regions — cardia, fundus, body, and pylorus — with the pyloric region housing the pyloric sphincter.

 

NOTE

 

• Gastrocnemius (Option 1): A major calf muscle in the leg, involved in walking and running, unrelated to digestion.

 

• Pectoralis (Option 2): A chest muscle involved in movement of the arm and shoulder, unrelated to digestion.

 

• Rectus (Option 3): Refers to muscles like the rectus abdominis ("abs") or rectus femoris (thigh); these support posture/movement, not regulation of food passage from stomach to intestine.

question: Which of the following awards is presented for lifetime achievement in sports and games? It was instituted to honour those sportspersons who have contributed to sports by their performance and continue to contribute to the promotion of sports even after their retirement from an active sporting career.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dhyanchand Award.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Dhyan Chand Award (instituted in 2002) is India's honour for lifetime achievement in sports, recognising sportspersons who have not only excelled in their playing careers but also continued to contribute to the promotion of sports after retirement. (ध्यानचंद पुरस्कार — आजीवन उपलब्धि)

 

• It is named after the legendary hockey player Major Dhyan Chand, celebrated for his extraordinary goal-scoring feats and contribution to India's hockey dominance in the early 20th century.

 

• The award is given by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, Government of India, and includes a statuette, certificate, ceremonial dress, and a cash prize.

 

• It is distinct from awards recognising current/recent outstanding performance, focusing instead on a sportsperson's overall, lasting contribution to their sport including post-retirement mentorship and development work.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's National Sports Day is celebrated on 29 August, the birth anniversary of Major Dhyan Chand, and is also the day major sports awards are conferred.

 

• The Arjuna Award recognises consistent outstanding performance in sports over a four-year period, and the Dronacharya Award honours excellence in coaching.

 

NOTE

 

• Arjuna Award (Option 1): Given for consistent excellent performance over a specified recent period, not specifically for lifetime achievement.

 

• Dronacharya Award (Option 3): Given to coaches for producing medal-winning sportspersons, not to athletes for their own performance.

 

• Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna (Option 4): India's highest annual sporting honour, awarded for the most outstanding performance in a recent period (renamed from the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna in 2021), rather than specifically for lifetime achievement after retirement.

question: What function does the public key serve in digital signature verification?
option_4: To calculate the hash value of the message or file content
solution_text:
The correct answer is To decrypt the digital signature.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In a digital signature scheme (based on asymmetric/public-key cryptography), the sender signs a message using their private key, and the recipient uses the sender's corresponding public key to decrypt/verify that signature. (डिजिटल हस्ताक्षर — सार्वजनिक कुंजी सत्यापन)

 

• Because the private key is kept secret and known only to the signer, successfully decrypting the signature with the signer's public key proves the message genuinely originated from that signer (authentication) and was not altered (integrity).

 

• The process typically works by the sender first computing a hash of the message, then encrypting that hash with their private key to create the digital signature; the receiver decrypts it using the public key and compares it with a freshly computed hash of the received message.

 

• If the decrypted value matches the recomputed hash, the signature is verified as valid; any mismatch indicates tampering or an invalid signature.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Common digital signature algorithms include RSA, DSA (Digital Signature Algorithm), and ECDSA (Elliptic Curve DSA).

 

• In India, digital signatures are legally recognised for authenticating electronic records under the Information Technology Act, 2000.

 

NOTE

 

• To ensure confidentiality during transmission (Option 1): Confidentiality is achieved by encrypting the message itself with the recipient's public key (a separate use of public-key cryptography), not by the digital signature process.

 

• To encrypt the digital signature (Option 2): It is the private key of the sender that is used to create (encrypt) the signature, not the public key.

 

• To calculate the hash value of the message or file content (Option 4): Hashing is performed by a hash function/algorithm (like SHA-256), independently of the public key, before the signing/verification step.

question: Which of the following is the official language of Afghanistan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dari.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dari (a variety of Persian/Farsi) is one of the two official languages of Afghanistan, alongside Pashto. (दारी — अफगानिस्तान की आधिकारिक भाषा)

 

• Dari serves as a lingua franca in Afghanistan and is widely used in government, media, and education, alongside Pashto.

 

• Afghanistan's capital is Kabul, and its currency is the Afghani.

 

• Other minority languages spoken in Afghanistan include Uzbek, Turkmen, Balochi, Pashayi, and Nuristani, but these do not hold official national status.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Pashto (the other official language) is spoken predominantly by the Pashtun ethnic group, Afghanistan's largest ethnic community.

 

• Afghanistan is a landlocked country in South-Central Asia, bordering Pakistan, Iran, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, and China.

 

NOTE

 

• Uzbek (Option 1): Spoken by the Uzbek minority in northern Afghanistan; a regional/minority language, not an official national language.

 

• Dhivehi (Option 2): The official language of the Maldives, unrelated to Afghanistan.

 

• Turkmen (Option 4): Spoken by the Turkmen minority in northern Afghanistan; a regional/minority language, not an official national language.

question: Bharatanatyam dance form is associated with:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bharatanatyam is one of the oldest classical dance forms of India and is traditionally associated with the state of Tamil Nadu. (भरतनाट्यम — तमिलनाडु)

 

• It originated in the Hindu temples of Tamil Nadu, historically performed by Devadasis, and follows the principles laid out in the ancient treatise Natya Shastra, attributed to sage Bharata.

 

• The dance form is characterised by fixed upper torso, bent legs and knees (aramandi), fast footwork, sculpturesque poses, and expressive hand gestures (mudras) combined with facial expressions (abhinaya).

 

• Prominent exponents of Bharatanatyam include Rukmini Devi Arundale, who revived and popularised the form in the 20th century, and dancers like Yamini Krishnamurthy and Padma Subrahmanyam.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Margazhi (Music and Dance) Season in Chennai, held every December-January, is a major festival prominently featuring Bharatanatyam performances.

 

• Other classical dance forms of India by state include: Kathak (Uttar Pradesh), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Odissi (Odisha), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Manipuri (Manipur), and Sattriya (Assam).

 

NOTE

 

• Karnataka (Option 1): Known for classical dance forms like Yakshagana, not Bharatanatyam.

 

• Himachal Pradesh (Option 3): Known for folk dances such as Nati, not a home to any of the eight recognised Indian classical dance forms.

 

• Haryana (Option 4): Known for folk dances such as Ghoomar and Phag, not associated with classical Bharatanatyam.

question: With which Gharana is the famous Tarana singer, Pandit Rattan Mohan Sharma associated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mewati Gharana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit Rattan Mohan Sharma, celebrated as a leading Tarana vocalist of Hindustani classical music, belongs to the Mewati Gharana. (मेवाती घराना — रतन मोहन शर्मा)

 

• He is the son of the noted vocalist Pandit Madhup Mudgal and trained within the Mewati Gharana's musical lineage, carrying forward its distinctive style of raga presentation.

 

• The Mewati Gharana is renowned for its rich, emotive vocal style and is closely linked to legendary figures such as Pandit Jasraj, one of its most famous exponents.

 

• Rattan Mohan Sharma has performed extensively in India and abroad and is associated with the Gandharva Mahavidyalaya, a well-known Delhi-based music institution founded by his family's musical tradition.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other well-known Hindustani vocal gharanas include the Kirana Gharana (Bhimsen Joshi, Gangubai Hangal) and the Gwalior Gharana, considered the oldest of the khyal gharanas.

 

• A tarana is a genre of fast, rhythmic Hindustani vocal composition set to nonsensical/Persian-Arabic-derived syllables rather than full lyrical text, showcasing vocal virtuosity.

 

NOTE

 

• Talwandi Gharana (Option 1): A gharana in Hindustani music but not the one associated with Rattan Mohan Sharma.

 

• Patiala Gharana (Option 2): Associated with vocalists like Bade Ghulam Ali Khan, not Rattan Mohan Sharma.

 

• Agra Gharana (Option 3): Associated with vocalists like Faiyaz Khan, not Rattan Mohan Sharma.

question: What is the minimum number of football players required in a team for a match to start?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 7.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• According to the Laws of the Game set by the International Football Association Board (IFAB), a football match requires each team to have a minimum of 7 players for the match to start or continue. (फुटबॉल — न्यूनतम 7 खिलाड़ी)

 

• While a standard team fields 11 players (including the goalkeeper), the match can proceed with fewer players due to injury, sending-off, or other reasons, as long as each side does not drop below seven.

 

• If a team's playing strength falls below 7 players, the referee must abandon the match.

 

• This rule ensures a match retains a minimum level of competitive fairness even when a team faces multiple player losses during the game.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• A standard football match, per the Laws of the Game, lasts 90 minutes, divided into two 45-minute halves.

 

• The football pitch dimensions and other match regulations are also standardised by FIFA, which adopts IFAB's Laws of the Game for its competitions.

 

NOTE

 

• 11 (Option 1): This is the standard/full squad size for kickoff, not the minimum required to start/continue a match.

 

• 8 (Option 2), 10 (Option 3): These are not the officially designated minimum player counts under the Laws of the Game.

question: The founder of the Pala empire was:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gopala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gopala founded the Pala Empire around 750 CE, establishing his rule over Bengal after being elected by regional chieftains to end a period of political anarchy known as "Matsyanyaya" (the law of the fish, where the strong devoured the weak). (गोपाल — पाल वंश के संस्थापक)

 

• Gopala's rise is notable as one of the few instances in Indian history where a ruler is recorded as having been elected to end anarchy, rather than seizing power purely by conquest or inheritance.

 

• The Pala dynasty went on to rule large parts of Bengal and Bihar for several centuries and became notable patrons of Buddhism, founding institutions like Vikramashila and Odantapuri universities.

 

• Gopala was succeeded by his son Dharmapala, who greatly expanded the empire and made it a dominant power in eastern and northern India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Dharmapala (Gopala's successor) and Devapala (Dharmapala's successor) further expanded the Pala Empire, involving it in the tripartite struggle for Kannauj against the Pratiharas and Rashtrakutas.

 

• The Palas were significant patrons of Mahayana and Vajrayana Buddhism, and Pala-era art and architecture influenced Buddhist traditions in Tibet and Southeast Asia.

 

NOTE

 

• Rayala (Option 1): Not a recognised Pala ruler; this name is associated with the Vijayanagara ruling title "Raya", an unrelated south Indian dynasty context.

 

• Devapala (Option 3): A later, powerful Pala ruler (grandson of Gopala), not the founder.

 

• Dharmapala (Option 4): Gopala's son and successor, who greatly expanded the empire, but not its founder.

question: ‘Tamu Lochar’ is one of the traditional festivals of the ____________ of Sikkim. It is celebrated to mark the beginning of their new year, which falls on the 15th day of Pusa, according to the Hindu calendar Vikram Samvat and 30th December in the English calendar.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gurung community.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Tamu Lochar" (Tamu Losar) is the traditional New Year festival of the Gurung community; "Tamu" is the name by which the Gurung people refer to themselves. (तमु ल्होछार — गुरुंग समुदाय)

 

• The festival is celebrated to mark the beginning of the Gurung New Year, which falls on the 15th day of the Pusa (Poush) month, corresponding to 30 December in the English (Gregorian) calendar.

 

• It is celebrated with great enthusiasm by the Gurung community in Sikkim, as well as in parts of Nepal, Darjeeling, and other regions with Gurung populations, featuring traditional dances, songs, and community feasts.

 

• The Gurung community follows the 12-year animal cycle (Tamu Sambat) calendar, similar to other Tibeto-Burman ethnic calendars, and Tamu Lochar marks the transition into a new year of this cycle.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sikkim also celebrates other New Year festivals tied to specific communities, such as Losoong/Namsoong (Bhutia community) and Sonam Lochar (Tamang community), each with its own distinct date and traditions.

 

• Sikkim is recognised for its rich multi-ethnic cultural diversity, with major communities including Lepcha, Bhutia, Gurung, Limbu, and Nepali-origin groups.

 

NOTE

 

• Mangar community (Option 1): A distinct ethnic community of Nepal/Sikkim with its own festivals, not associated with Tamu Lochar.

 

• Bhutia community (Option 2): Celebrates their own New Year festival, Losoong, not Tamu Lochar.

 

• Lepcha community (Option 3): Sikkim's indigenous community, celebrates Namsoong as their New Year, not Tamu Lochar.
